transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Jared Martin (Redwood AE), Priya Singh (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Redwood CSM), Elena Torres (Spectral CISO), Markus Chen (Infra Lead), Rashida Karim (Compliance), Omar Diaz (DevOps)

Summary:
Quick posture review for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 readiness; confirm Trust Center access path, controls mapping for data residency, RBAC/SSO expectations, and high-level KMS/encryption integration. Agreed to exchange redacted reports and run a short KMS design spike.

Topics:
- Trust Center access & reports
- Controls mapping (SOC 2 / ISO) to Spectral's control matrix
- RBAC/SSO & SAML provisioning
- Audit logs & retention / evidence export
- Data residency and Dedicated vs Private deployment tradeoffs
- KMS / encryption & key rotation

Action items (captured above)

Transcript:
[00:00] Jared: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — I think we got all the right folks from Spectral, Elena, hi.
[00:08] Elena: Hi Jared, thanks. Quick note, we had a conflict earlier so appreciate you shifting.
[00:12] Jared: No worries. Priya, do you want to kick us off with the high level of what we plan to show today?
[00:16] Priya: Sure, quick agenda — we'll run through how Redwood exposes assurance artifacts, show the Trust Center flow for read-only access, then map the common SOC 2/ISO controls to what Spectral is asking for — especially around audit logs, SSO/RBAC, and KMS. We'll leave time for Q&A and then next steps.
[00:33] Markus: Sounds good. Nominally our main constraint is data residency for EU customers, and we need to ensure keys never leave our control for certain datasets.
[00:41] Rashida: And from compliance side we need evidence export for 12 months of audit logs plus change history for RBAC changes.
[00:48] Priya: Got it. We often see that mapping split into two buckets: platform-managed artifacts (SOC 2 report, ISO summary, control descriptions) and per-tenant access (audit exports, KMS flows). We'll show both.
[01:05] [auto-note slight cut] Jared: Quick clarifier, when we say KMS integration — you mean customer-managed keys in your cloud K M S and not Redwood-managed?
[01:14] Elena: Correct, we want BYOK for PII datasets.
[01:17] Priya: Great. On Redwood Private and Dedicated we support both patterns. For Private we can do a customer-managed KMS and full key ownership (we don't persist plaintext). For Dedicated we offer KMS integrations that can be configured per-reservation — but I should show the diagram.
[01:33] [02:00] Priya: (shares screens) Okay I have the Trust Center UI up — apologies if the recording blurs some of the screen text. In the Trust Center you'll see a section labeled "Compliance artifacts" where redacted SOC 2 Type II and the ISO27001 certificate summary live. There's an access control toggle so you can add Spectral's auditors as read-only.
[02:20] Omar: Is the evidence download audit-traceable? We need chain of custody for who accessed what and when.
[02:26] Priya: Yes, there's an access audit log — every Trust Center download event is captured and surfaced in the tenant audit log. That log itself can be exported as newline-delimited JSON. Note: retention defaults to 12 months for Hosted but we can extend under enterprise contracts.
[02:41] Elena: Can we map which SOC control maps to which endpoint e.g., audit log retention -> CC6.1 or whatever — we need a controls crosswalk.
[02:49] Jared: We prepared a controls map template — we'll share a CSV that maps SOC 2 and ISO clauses to Redwood artifacts and configuration knobs (RBAC, audit logs, data residency).
[02:56] Markus: Great — one practical item: for residency-bound traffic we need a predictable egress path so data never goes to non-EU regions even for fallback. How does auto-failover routing handle that?
[03:06] Priya: Good question. We have routing policies that can be pinned by region; for Dedicated you can pin a pool in eu-west and configure a strict policy which blocks cross-region fallback. For Hosted we default to cross-region fallback for availability unless you enable residency-only mode (that's part of Dedicated/private offers). There's a small SLO tradeoff but it's explicit.
[03:30] Rashida: We need that in writing — the control we map will be 'no cross-border transfer' and we need the exact configuration names and any exceptions.
[03:38] Jared: We'll add the config names to the crosswalk doc.
[03:41] [04:00] Elena: On RBAC and SSO — how granular is role mapping? We want per-team roles, and changes must be auditable.
[04:08] Priya: We integrate with SAML 2.0 / SCIM provisioning. Roles are mapped to groups and each role change emits an event into the audit log. The UI has role templates (Reader, Writer, Admin) — and we support custom roles with scope down to model-route level.
[04:26] Omar: SCIM provisioning cadence — is it near-real-time or periodic sync?
[04:31] Priya: It's near-real-time; SCIM push handles adds/updates/removes and we log the delta. Occasionally the provisioning provider will debounce rapid changes which shows as a short delay, but it's typically within seconds to a minute.
[04:45] [05:00] Elena: For evidence we need immutable snapshots from the logs for a period — we can't accept overwritten logs. Is log immutability supported?
[05:08] Priya: The audit logs are append-only in our storage tier and we provide signed hashes for exported bundles so you can verify integrity. For Private we can integrate with your log archiving solution (S3 with Object Lock) to provide WORM-like behavior.
[05:24] Markus: Excellent. Can we pull ad-hoc exports for a given date range and include RBAC change history for that period?
[05:30] Priya: Yes, the export supports time ranges and can include context blobs (like request headers, route config, and RBAC deltas). There's a size limit on the export—large ranges will be chunked but we provide a manifest.
[05:45] [06:00] Jared: Let's talk about the SOC 2 artifacts — Elena, do you want the full Type II or a redacted copy?
[06:06] Elena: Redacted first, internal audit wants to validate scope and frequency before we request the full one.
[06:12] Jared: Okay we'll provide redacted. The standard package includes the auditor's opinion, control descriptions, and test sample summary.
[06:20] Rashida: For ISO we need the scope statement and list of controls mapped to ISO clauses, not the full certificate necessarily.
[06:26] Priya: We can also provide the control implementation narratives that speak to how we perform key management and encryption.
[06:32] [07:00] Elena: About encryption in transit and at rest — we need TLS details and cipher suites, plus any hardware security module usage.
[07:08] Priya: TLS 1.2+ supported, we recommend TLS1.3; cipher suite list is in the Trust Center doc. HSM — for Private we can front your KMS which in turn is backed by HSM-managed keys; for Redwood-managed keys we use cloud KMS with customer-tenant isolation and we rotate keys on a schedule but we also support customer-managed keys where you keep control.
[07:28] Markus: Key rotation window? Do you offer automated key rotation or is it manual?
[07:33] Priya: Both. You can set scheduled rotation and also rotate on-demand. For BYOK we honor your cloud provider rotation policies.
[07:39] [08:00] Omar: Small concern: when you say "we don't persist plaintext" can you clarify at which points the model cache might store intermediate representations? Is KV cache encrypted?
[08:09] Priya: Good callout. The serving runtime uses an encrypted KV cache in memory; for persistence layers the cache is encrypted at rest and access controlled. We can provide a flow diagram with the cache lifecycle. Sometimes transcripts show "K V" as separate tokens but the important piece is the cache is not stored in plaintext on disk in Private or Dedicated deployments.
[08:34] Rashida: We'll want that diagram as part of the crosswalk.
[08:39] [09:00] Jared: Switching gears to evidence collection — for audits we typically give a zip with the SOC 2 artifacts, the export manifest, and signed log bundles. The Trust Center allows a reviewer role with time-limited access.
[09:10] Elena: Can we create a reviewer with access only to artifacts and not production APIs?
[09:15] Priya: Yes, reviewer role is read-only limited to Trust Center and artifact download — no API keys.
[09:20] Markus: Any additional controls for dev/staging vs prod separation? We prefer network isolation for staging.
[09:26] Priya: We recommend separate projects/namespaces per environment; we can enforce network policies and private endpoints so staging has its own VPC-peered path.
[09:35] [10:00] Elena: A question on attestation — does Redwood publish a SOC 2 scope statement that lists excluded systems? We need to know the exact boundary.
[10:08] Jared: Yes, the SOC scope includes the inference runtime, control plane, and data paths for hosted customers — but not third-party analytics providers you choose to integrate. We'll attach the scope page.
[10:19] Rashida: Please call out the retained log storage provider and any subprocessors.
[10:23] Priya: We'll provide a subprocessors list in the Trust Center; for log storage we use cloud provider managed storage in-region unless otherwise specified.
[10:33] [11:00] [brief crosstalk]
[11:20] Omar: For residency, does the Dedicated pool support strict egress filtering (no outbound to non-EU) even for system telemetry?
[11:27] Priya: We can configure telemetry collection endpoints to be region-bound; some operational telemetry is optional and can be disabled or proxied to your telemetry collector. We'll note that in the config sheet.
[11:41] [12:00] Elena: On the legal side we may have to present a data processing addendum (DPA). Do you have a standard DPA with SCCs?
[12:09] Jared: Yes — we have an EU addendum and we can add SCCs or local clauses as required for enterprise.
[12:16] Rashida: We might need the DPA redline before next Friday.
[12:20] Jared: We'll route that to Legal — Jared will be the contact.
[12:26] [13:00] Priya: Short demo note — when you go into the Trust Center -> Artifacts -> Exports, you can request an export and we queue it; for large exports we provide a signed URL to a chunked manifest. Each chunk is individually signed.
[13:42] Markus: That signing — what algorithm do you use for the manifest signing? We need SHA-2 family specifics.
[13:49] Priya: We use SHA-256 signatures and the signature metadata is included in the manifest.
[13:55] [14:00] Elena: For ISO control mapping, do you have prebuilt mappings or is it custom per customer?
[14:06] Priya: We have a prebuilt map that covers the common ISO clauses and SOC 2 CC criteria; we then provide a customer-specific column where we tie your config and artifacts to the clause.
[14:18] Omar: Any gotchas with SCIM group names syncing weird characters? We've seen UTF normalization issues.
[14:24] Priya: We normalize to NFC and strip control chars; we'll include that in the provisioning notes.
[14:34] [15:00] Elena: Are there any known gaps we should be aware of for SOC 2 — e.g., some providers don't include operational penetration testing in scope.
[15:08] Jared: Our SOC 2 includes annual pen tests as described in the report; if you need third-party attestations more often we can discuss contractual add-ons.
[15:18] Rashida: Also interested in MFA enforcement for admin roles — does Redwood enforce MFA?
[15:23] Priya: Yes MFA is required for admin-privileged users and we support hardware keys (FIDO) for higher assurance.
[15:30] [16:00] Markus: Let's talk throughput/latency for Dedicated if we run a residency-only pool — we need a perf SLA for in-region requests; will that be the same as hosted?
[16:09] Jared: Dedicated SLAs are contractual and typically include a latency SLO per model class — we'll provide the SLO table in the contract; the important piece is that residency-only Dedicated pools can be sized to meet your throughput.
[16:23] Omar: For the spike test we want to see the audit logs show 1:1 mapping of request->token spikes for cost reconciliation.
[16:30] Priya: We'll capture that in the benchmark. We'll share a sample spreadsheet with token counts and latency percentiles.
[16:40] [17:00] Elena: A smaller but crucial ask: are backups of KMS keys accessible to Redwood staff? We need strict separation.
[17:08] Priya: For BYOK, Redwood operators cannot access key material. For Redwood-managed keys, we have restricted operator access and all key operations are logged. We'll provide the access control narrative.
[17:22] Rashida: Can you provide proof of operator access reviews?
[17:26] Jared: Yes, operator access review artifacts are part of the auditor package and we'll include the cadence.
[17:33] [18:00] Priya: (moves to the controls crosswalk sample) Here's how we lay it out: Column A: Control name, Column B: SOC/ISO reference, Column C: Redwood artifact/config, Column D: Evidence path (Trust Center URL or export name).
[18:49] Markus: That CSV will be helpful.
[18:53] [19:00] Elena: Any vendor subprocessors for telemetry or analytics? We need exact names for our vendor inventory.
[19:06] Priya: We'll list them — e.g., cloud provider region storage, CDN provider, and a small analytics vendor used for aggregated anonymized metrics. All are documented.
[19:18] Omar: About log retention — is it configurable per log type? Eg: auth logs 13 months, request logs 6 months?
[19:25] Priya: Yes retention can be configured per log stream under Dedicated/Private; hosted has defaults but can be extended.
[19:33] [20:00] Jared: Let's capture the open concerns: data residency enforcement, KMS BYOK proof, audit log immutability, provisioning cadence, SCIM normalization, DPA redline. Anything else?
[20:14] Elena: Also reviewer-only access to artifacts.
[20:18] Jared: Good. We'll include all that in the next steps.
[20:22] [21:00] Rashida: One last nit: for incident response do you provide timelines for notification? Our policy needs 72-hour breach notification.
[21:31] Priya: We have an incident response SLA and will notify relevant contacts; the DPA can specify 72 hours for incidents affecting data in-scope.
[21:41] [22:00] Jared: Closing summary — we'll: 1) Share redacted SOC 2 + ISO summary and control narratives; 2) Provide the Trust Center read-only access for your reviewers; 3) Priya will draft KMS integration flow; 4) Schedule a short dedicated performance/security spike; 5) Share DPA redline to Rashida.
[22:25] Elena: That's good. When can we expect the docs?
[22:28] Jared: We'll get the redacted reports and trust center link by 2027-09-10, Priya's KMS note by 9/15, and we'll tentatively schedule the spike for the week of 2027-09-20.
[22:40] Omar: Thanks all.
[22:42] [end approx 15:48 UTC? transcription drift]

Notes on transcription quality: occasional mis-hear of acronyms (SCIM shown as S-CIM in places), brief overlap/crosstalk at timestamps, some UI labels blurred in screen share.

Shared artifacts mentioned:
- Controls crosswalk CSV (to be shared)

Recap / Next steps (verbatim):
- Jared: I'll share the redacted SOC 2 and Trust Center link by 2027-09-10.
- Priya: I'll send the KMS integration flow and a short notes doc by 2027-09-15.
- Rashida: We'll provide control list in-scope by 2027-09-12.

End of transcript.
